flawed_step: Lines 0165–0182: the inversion theorem is stated without the necessary hypothesis α(1) ≠ 0, although β(1)=1/α(1) and the proof requires a nonsingular system.
counterexample: Let α(n)=0 for every positive integer n and let G(t)=1 for every t>0. Define F as required by line 0167. Then F(X)=Σ_{n≤X}0·G(X/n)=0 for every X, so the theorem's premise holds. At X=1, G(1)=1 and F(1)=0. But the prescribed coefficient is β(1)=1/α(1)=1/0, which is undefined. Moreover, no finite β(1) could make the asserted identity hold, since it would require 1=G(1)=β(1)F(1)=β(1)·0=0.
assessment_summary: The first substantive theorem already fails as stated because it omits α(1)≠0. The explicit α≡0 example satisfies its premise but makes the proposed inverse undefined and recovery of G impossible.
